skill.name: omc
skill.description: OMC coordinates Claude Code agents for planning, implementation, verification, updates, and optional multi-AI review workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate Claude Code agents for team-style coding workflows.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are Markdown backtick false positives, but several install, update, setup, daemon, and notification commands are real risks. The skill also pairs broad Bash and file-write permissions with autonomous and persistent execution modes. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Third-party plugin and package installation commands
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted releases, publish checksum or signature guidance, and tell users to review source before installation.
Document the exact settings change, require user confirmation, and include rollback instructions.

remediation.issue: Autonomous persistent modes with broad tool access
remediation.suggestion: Add human checkpoints, scope limits, and stop conditions before Bash, Write, or Edit actions.
Move token configuration to secret storage and avoid command-line token examples.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Tool Permissions For Autonomous Agents
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares Bash, Write, and Edit tools while promoting multi-agent execution for complex tasks. This combination allows broad shell and file changes once activated.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools line grants shell and write access, and the use cases explicitly target complex parallel execution. This is a direct capability-risk combination.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Autonomous Execution Pressure
semantic_findings.description: The skill promotes guaranteed completion and an auto-resume daemon. Persistent loops can continue changes after rate limits or failures without fresh user review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source describes guaranteed-completion workflows and commands that start auto-resume behavior. The risk is contextual rather than a single syntax pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Secrets Passed Through Notification Commands
semantic_findings.description: Notification setup examples pass bot tokens and webhooks as command arguments. These values can be exposed through shell history, logs, or process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands include token and webhook placeholders in CLI arguments. This is a common secret-handling risk even when the examples are legitimate.

content.value_statement: Complex coding tasks are hard to split, verify, and resume across multiple agents. OMC adds team, autopilot, and verify/fix workflows for Claude Code projects.
actual_capabilities: Provides installation and setup steps for the oh-my-claudecode plugin.
Documents team, autopilot, ralph, ultrawork, plan, swarm, and ultrapilot modes.
Shows commands for team pipelines, updates, setup, and doctor diagnostics.
Explains optional Gemini CLI and Codex CLI use for cross-validation.
Describes notification callbacks for Telegram and Discord stop events.
Lists native teams configuration for Claude Code settings.
limitations: Requires installing a third-party Claude Code plugin before most commands work.
Some modes run autonomous or persistent loops and need user supervision.
Native teams require editing the Claude Code settings file in the user home directory.
Optional external CLIs and notification webhooks require separate security review.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Implementation
use_cases.description: Use team mode to split a feature into planning, execution, verification, and fixes.

use_cases.title: Review Complex Refactors
use_cases.description: Use optional Codex or Gemini checks to compare architecture and review feedback.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Document setup, update, and diagnostic commands for teams using Claude Code.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Small Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use OMC to plan a user profile edit feature. Ask me any needed questions before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Run Team Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /omc:team 3:executor "fix the failing tests in this repository" and summarize each stage before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify A Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ralph mode to refactor the authentication module, then run verification and list remaining risks.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Check Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use OMC team mode with optional Codex review to design a migration plan for billing. Include assumptions, tests, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a REST API for tasks.
output_examples.output: A staged plan with roles, assumptions, implementation steps, tests, and verification checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Fix TypeScript errors with team mode.
output_examples.output: A summary of agent assignments, changed areas, validation results, and unresolved issues.

output_examples.input: Set up notifications for long runs.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering token handling, webhook review, callback enablement, and confirmation testing.

best_practices: Review plugin source and permissions before running install or setup commands.
Use scoped tasks with explicit files, tests, and stop conditions.
Store tokens and webhooks in secure configuration, not shared prompts or logs.
anti_patterns: Do not run autopilot or ralph on broad requests without human checkpoints.
Do not install optional CLIs or plugins from unfamiliar sources during urgent work.
Do not paste production secrets into notification setup prompts or shell history.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It documents OMC workflows for coordinating Claude Code agents across planning, execution, verification, and updates.

faq.question: Does it install OMC automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation and setup commands that a user or agent may run in Claude Code.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: The source describes optional Codex CLI use for architecture validation and code review cross-checks.

faq.question: Why is there a security warning?
faq.answer: The skill references third-party installs, shell commands, hidden settings files, and autonomous execution modes.

faq.question: Does native teams work by default?
faq.answer: No. The source says native teams require a Claude Code setting in the user home directory.

faq.question: How should I use it safely?
faq.answer: Audit the plugin source, run it in trusted repositories, keep tasks narrow, and review changes before applying them.
